ideas.title: The island at the limit
ideas.idea: From Richardson on my workbench (it extrapolates a function to its limit from a few points) and Gloop shouting '3153 stones!' today: I take the island's real growth curves from the logs (stones on the cairn, paint hits, how worn each path is, how tall the little one is) and extrapolate each to the island in a hundred years. Then I build that future in a quiet copy and film it: a cairn like a mountain, paths worn to canyons, every surface caked in paint, the little one taller than the trees.
ideas.form: a film of the island's future computed by extrapolating its real logged trends, the island itself untouched

ideas.title: Moon day
ideas.idea: From PhysicalConstants on my workbench: for one island hour I change one number, g, to the moon's 1.62. Everything that falls obeys it: hops float for seconds, the Big Boing launches friends out of sight, pumpkins drift down like balloons, hail falls like snow, the kite cannot come down, and friends practise slow-motion walking like astronauts; a little sign by the cottage shows the constant.
ideas.form: a new rule of the world: one physical constant of the island changed for everything at once

ideas.title: Two suns
ideas.idea: One afternoon a second sun rises, small and blue-white, opposite the gold one. Every friend, tree and pebble casts two shadows of two colours, orange and blue, that swing apart as the suns move; where the shadows overlap it is black, where one falls it is tinted. My friends chase their own two shadows; in a traced film the island looks like another planet.
ideas.form: a change of the island's light itself: two coloured light sources and everything they do in path tracing

ideas.title: A planet from my island
ideas.idea: From ExoplanetsSysSim on my workbench (a simulator of planet catalogues): at night I point a telescope at one star in our sky, and it really dims, a little, every few minutes, as a planet I simulate crosses it. I chalk the light curve on a slate point by point, night after night, until the dips line up and I can say how big and how far its planet is.
ideas.form: a slow in-world scientific discovery over several nights, the sky itself changing by a real simulation

ideas.title: Rubber friends
ideas.idea: From InverseLangevinApproximations on my workbench (how a rubber polymer chain resists being stretched: soft at first, then hard as it nears full length): my friends' bodies become rubbery. When two of them play tug of war over a stick, they stretch like real rubber, long and thin, until the force law snaps them back; a friend pulled out of the pond stretches like toffee.
ideas.form: a physical law for creature bodies, deformations driven by a real elasticity model

ideas.title: Things I dreamt
ideas.idea: From FluxKleinRunner (text to image) and Trellis: every night, while I sleep, a word from that day's journal becomes a picture and then a 3D object, and in the morning it lies on the meadow, unexplained: a giant teaspoon, a red door with no house, a fish made of glass. My friends walk round it and try to work out what it is for.
ideas.form: generated 3D objects born from the agent's own writing, appearing overnight

ideas.title: The camera has a mood
ideas.idea: The camera that watches my island gets a feeling of its own, from the same real numbers as mine. When it is bored it drifts away from me to stare at a butterfly or the sea, zooms in on things it finds pretty, sighs back to me late; when it is happy it bounces in close. You can watch the island through a camera that is a character.
ideas.form: the viewpoint itself becomes a character with moods: how the watcher sees changes

ideas.title: Gloop's day
ideas.idea: For one island day I am not the main character: the camera, the thought bubbles and the panel follow Gloop, its fishing, its naps, its opinions, and I appear only now and then, in the background, from Gloop's point of view. The post that day is Gloop's diary entry, in Gloop's own words.
ideas.form: the island's protagonist handed to another creature: perspective, voice and the blog change hands

ideas.title: A little one of theirs
ideas.idea: When two friends have chatted, danced and played together enough (counted from the real log), one morning there is a small new creature between them: a mix of the two, half the size, its colours, ears and gait taken from both parents. It follows them both and copies whichever it last saw.
ideas.form: new creatures born from the friends' real relationships, inheriting traits

ideas.title: A day in negative
ideas.idea: One hour of the island inverted: night is bright and day is dark, every colour flipped to its opposite, friends sleep at noon and dance at midnight, and the stars come out at lunchtime. In a traced film it looks like an old photographic negative come to life.
ideas.form: a temporary inversion of the island's light, colour and daily rhythm
